notes: rounds/tester.py record_result reads the tester's row through own_result and runs refusal() (non-Open round, superseded build, and on POST a submitted result) for GET and again under the round lock for POST; form_for gives a submitted result no form, and results.save_result fetches the row by tester again before writing. M1 drops the tester filter in own_result and save_result, so another tester's draft is shown and overwritten; M3 lets refusal() pass a Closed round; M4 removes the submitted refusal, gives a submitted result a form, shows that form in tester_result.html and prints the real status there (a save keeps submitted_at, so it stays Submitted). ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint); the observation is RoundTextField(max_length=2000, optional=True), whose message is built from max_length, so M5's message also says 2001. M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005_result to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
